correctness.rationale: For a>=2,b>=a-1, the weighted matrix-tree Schur complement gives a^(b-1)(prod y_i)(a t+sum y_i)^(a-1), hence an exact multinomial law for K clique edges and B-vertex degree excesses. The favorable condition K=0 and no B-degree above 2 bijects uniformly with a labeled Cayley tree, injectively distinct B edge-subdivision labels and independent uniform attachments of remaining B leaves. Therefore Q=P(.|E), dTV=1-(b)_(a-1)/(a+b)^(a-1) exactly. Log expansion gives b~a² transition and iff b/a²→infinity for a→infinity, while the joint occupancy factorial-moment argument gives independent Poisson(λ) clique-edge and Poisson(λ/2) collision defects. The two-marked Cayley path formula gives Rayleigh distances under Q, transferred to P when total variation→0. Independently enumerated all spanning trees using Prüfer sequences for (a,b)=(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3) and checked total and favorable counts; actual verify.py inspected. Classical enumerator and Rayleigh facts are credited, not claimed original.
residual_risks: Poisson independence argument relies on the factorial-moment cluster exclusion in the supplied proof, not independently computed unbounded occupancy certificates.

originality.rationale: The forward degree-weighted multipartite enumerator is classical (Clark; Klee–Stamps) and already entails the occupancy polynomial, so cannot itself be claimed. The surviving full-tree geometry claim is the exact conditional decorated Cayley model and its optimal TV threshold, independent two-defect critical law, and marked-distance transfer. The same-day published result on random subtrees of complete split graphs studies omitted vertices under b/a proportional and not spanning-tree clique-degree defects. A 1994 multipartite-tree bijection and a 2023 forest containment article remain partially inaccessible and are material priority risks, but no demonstrated stronger covering statement was found.
